title: Max builds a house that floats (it floated away first)

beats.text: Max finally built a house that floats. Now it's floating away.
Let's rewind to his very first riverside cabin.
Max builds his cabin on a plain slab. The river never gets this high, he says. One metre inside, the sofa floats by.
So he builds a hollow pontoon in a wet dock. A cubic metre of water weighs a tonne: displace your weight, and you float.
But nothing holds it. Max drifts out of his dock and away across the river, still waving.
Four guide posts with collars on the corners: now it only moves straight up and down.
Next flood, it rises nicely, but the rigid pipe and cable are fixed to the ground. Gusher, sparks, lights out.
Coiled flexible lines with three metres of slack simply stretch as the house rises.
Then Max loads a bathtub, piano and bookcase against one wall. Top-heavy, it leans and scrapes the posts.
Heavy ballast goes low and centred in the pontoon. Now it floats perfectly level.
The big flood rises 2.7 metres. The house rises level and lit, the kids eating cake inside. Maasbommel has 32 of these. Would you live in one?

overlay.text: 32 floating homes in Maasbommel can rise
